title: Review check becomes a reusable workflow
summary: The review check moves out of osf's own `review.yml` into a reusable `review-check.yml` that any repository can call, and osf's caller shrinks to a single `uses:` job. The build job no longer compiles osf from the pull request's base branch — which can be any branch — but from the workflow's own trusted commit, verified against `job.workflow_sha`/`job.workflow_repository`; the base commit is now only the diff target. Settings that were repository variables become `workflow_call` inputs and secrets, so a caller passes them explicitly. On the osf side, `review reduce` accepts a folder of saved reviewer files, and `PullRequest::load` accepts a raw code-host event file, so the workflow can hand over `GITHUB_EVENT_PATH` directly.

lanes.label: Caller
lanes.subtitle: pull_request_target, default branch
lanes.summary: The workflow GitHub reads from the default branch. osf's own caller is now one job that only calls the reusable workflow; an adopter's caller names it by full commit SHA.

lanes.label: Review check
lanes.subtitle: reusable workflow jobs
lanes.summary: The reusable workflow that holds every job: build, one job per reviewer, the deciding job, and the fork-disabled job.

lanes.label: osf binary
lanes.subtitle: Rust CLI, built from the pinned commit
lanes.summary: The tool the jobs run. Its review subcommands read the pull request, run a reviewer, and reduce the saved answers.

lanes.label: External
lanes.subtitle: GitHub, registries, model providers
lanes.summary: The code host, the container registry, and the model providers each reviewer job reaches.

nodes.label: review.yml
nodes.subtitle: one job, no steps
nodes.summary: osf's own caller. It triggers on pull_request_target, grants the union of the called jobs' read permissions, and calls the reusable workflow by local path at the same commit. It passes `osf-ref: github.workflow_sha`, `osf-repository: github.repository`, the runner label, the verifier app id, and `allow-forks` from the repository variable.

nodes.label: Adopter caller
nodes.subtitle: names the check by 40-char SHA
nodes.summary: A caller in another repository names `review-check.yml` by a full commit SHA and passes the same SHA as `osf-ref`, mapping each secret by name or using `secrets: inherit` within one organization.

nodes.label: review-check.yml
nodes.subtitle: on: workflow_call
nodes.summary: The reusable workflow. It declares the stable inputs `osf-ref`, `osf-repository`, `runs-on`, `verifier-app-id` and `allow-forks`, and the secrets `VERIFIER_APP_PRIVATE_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` and `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`. It reads no repository variable.

nodes.label: build job
nodes.subtitle: no secret, read-only token
nodes.summary: Checks out the pinned osf at `osf-ref` into `osf-src`, refuses any ref that is not a full SHA or that differs from `job.workflow_sha`/`job.workflow_repository`, builds it with no cache into `build-out`, and runs `osf review work-item` to find the issue the pull request names.

nodes.label: reviewer jobs
nodes.subtitle: codex, claude, opencode
nodes.summary: One job per reviewer, each with only its own provider key and an egress allow-list of its provider's host plus the hosts it needs. Each checks out the caller's base for trusted config and the pull request's head as data, then runs `osf review run --reviewer <name> --if-enabled`.

nodes.label: review job
nodes.subtitle: decides and posts
nodes.summary: Collects every `review-run-*` artifact, mints the verifier app token, and runs `osf review reduce` over the downloaded folder, writing SARIF and posting the review. It runs even when a reviewer job failed.

nodes.label: review-fork-disabled
nodes.subtitle: fails loudly
nodes.summary: Runs for a fork's pull request when `allow-forks` is false, with no permissions and every endpoint blocked, and fails rather than skipping so an unconfigured fork cannot pass the check.

nodes.label: osf CLI
nodes.subtitle: review run | reduce | work-item
nodes.summary: The binary the build job produces and every later job runs. `review reduce` now expands a folder argument into the `.json` files directly inside it, sorted by name.

nodes.label: expand_saved_runs
nodes.subtitle: fn expand_saved_runs(&[PathBuf]) -> Result<Vec<PathBuf>, String>
nodes.summary: A path that is a directory stands for the `.json` files directly inside it, sorted by name; anything else is passed through unchanged. This lets the workflow hand `review reduce` the folder it downloaded instead of listing files.

nodes.label: PullRequest::load
nodes.subtitle: fn load(path: &Path) -> Result<PullRequest, String>
nodes.summary: Reads the pull request from a JSON file that is either the flat number/title/body object or a code-host event file that nests them under `pull_request`. The workflow can now pass `GITHUB_EVENT_PATH` straight through.

nodes.label: credential note
nodes.subtitle: prepare_command
nodes.summary: When a reviewer's credential variable is empty or unset, the run records a note naming the variable, so a selected reviewer with no key is legible as could-not-run rather than silent.

nodes.label: review_workflow tests
nodes.subtitle: reads both workflow files as text
nodes.summary: The integration tests now read `review-check.yml` for the jobs and `review.yml` for the caller, and assert the stable input list, the declared secrets, the pinned osf ref, the fixed environments, and that the caller is thin.

nodes.label: GitHub API
nodes.subtitle: issues, pull requests, checks
nodes.summary: Read by the build job's read-only token to find the work item, and written by the verifier app token in the last job to post the review.

nodes.label: ghcr.io
nodes.subtitle: devcontainer image by digest
nodes.summary: Every job logs in and pulls the same digest-pinned review image, which carries the Rust toolchain and the reviewer tools.

nodes.label: Model providers
nodes.subtitle: openai, anthropic, openrouter
nodes.summary: Each reviewer job reaches only its own provider's host, plus the hosts its agent needs to start, through the egress allow-list.

edges.label: uses: ./review-check.yml
edges.summary: The caller holds no step of its own; it hands the whole check to the reusable workflow at the same commit.

edges.label: @<40-char SHA>
edges.summary: An adopter's caller pins the jobs by commit SHA and passes the same SHA as `osf-ref`, so the code that runs beside the keys is fixed.

edges.label: cargo build --release --bin osf
edges.summary: The build job compiles osf from the pinned checkout into `build-out`, then runs `osf review work-item` from the read-only build output.

edges.label: osf review run --reviewer <name>
edges.summary: Each reviewer job runs the built binary against the base checkout and the pull request's head, with only its own provider key in the environment.

edges.label: osf review reduce /out/runs
edges.summary: The last job passes the downloaded folder of saved answers; `expand_saved_runs` turns it into the reviewer files.
`review reduce` expands each folder argument before reading the runs.
`load_pull_request` now delegates to `PullRequest::load`, which unwraps an event file's nested `pull_request`.
A reviewer whose key is empty runs anyway and records a note naming the variable, which the aggregate verdict reads as could-not-run.
The tests read the reusable workflow as text and assert its inputs, secrets, pins and environments.
The tests read the caller as text and assert it is thin, has no step, and passes only declared inputs.

edges.label: read-only token
edges.summary: The build job's token reads issues and pull requests only, to find the work item the pull request names.

edges.label: docker login + pull
edges.summary: Every job logs in with its own token and pulls the digest-pinned review image.

edges.label: one provider host each
edges.summary: Each reviewer job's egress allow-list names only its provider's host plus the hosts its agent needs to start.

edges.label: verifier app token
edges.summary: The last job alone mints the verifier app token and posts the review and check run.
